assessments.reasoning: agpl_terms [4078,4286) places the positive copying-enablement test immediately before the narrow exclusion. Reading both sentences rules out treating every network transaction without a recorded download as exempt.

challenge.method: Compared using a remote program without receiving its code with the same service also supplying a downloadable copy of the program. Tested whether the §0 exclusion defeats §13.
challenge.results: Remote use alone falls within the exclusion. Supplying a working download enables copying and can constitute conveying even without evidence that a user completed the download. Independently, remote use can trigger the §13 offer for a qualifying modified version even when the interaction conveys no copy.

limitations: The exclusion concerns the interaction itself. An accompanying download and any applicable §13 source offer require separate analysis.
reasoning: AGPLv3 §0 excludes mere network interaction without transfer of a copy from conveying. The preceding definition includes propagation that enables another party to make or receive a copy.
